title: Reaching for the stars
caption: Antu, and Yepun's lasers beneath the Milky Way, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Against a dark sky, Unit Telescope 1, known as Antu, takes center stage at ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT). Behind it hides a near-identical twin, UT4 or Yepun, sending its laser beams up toward the stars, while the Milky Way stretches low along the horizon. Chilean astrophotographer Alexis Trigo captured the scene.
The VLT has four Unit Telescopes, each with a mirror 8.2 m across and a dome as big as a family house that shields it from the elements. Yepun stands apart as the only one carrying four lasers.

The lasers make artificial stars in Earth's upper atmosphere, letting astronomers measure and correct the turbulence that blurs their data. At first only UT4 had lasers. That changed recently when the VLT Interferometer's GRAVITY+ upgrade was completed, adding a laser to each of the other three. Even so, Yepun's set of four keeps it distinctive.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph by Alexis Trigo. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the laser beams and the Milky Way may look brighter here than to someone standing nearby.
